correctness.rationale: Exact factorization gives only rational roots and degree 255. Over F_2 all coefficients equal 1 by (1+X)^255 = (1+X^256)/(1+X). Over F_5 the Frobenius factorization is A(X)A(X^5)B(X^25)(1+X^125), A coefficients (1,1,3,3,1,1), B=(1,1,1,1,1). Interior coefficients and all overlap sums (3,2,1,1,2,3) are nonzero. Replayed standalone verification.py checks all 256 coefficients by a separate direct modular multiplication algorithm and exact factorization, with residues 1:74,3:102,7:20,9:60. The lower bound follows for any hypothetical degree upper bound.

value.rationale: This construction answers a direct numerical feasibility question arising from the explicit two-prime open Problem 1 of the 2023 paper: the bound for pair {2,3} is sharp at 3, while any analogous 2-and-5 bound must be at least 255. Its 256 simultaneous unit-coefficient conditions cannot be inferred from the parity lemma alone; a four-scale Frobenius decomposition proves every modular overlap is nonzero. This is a concrete, structurally motivated lower-bound obstruction, not an arbitrary slice or routine numerical substitution. It does not settle finiteness and carries no claim of a record bound.
